title: Characters such as "ɑ̄" cannot be displayed correctly.

judgment.rationale: The author already answered the font and subset questions, and a later commenter supplies a Chinese-locale combining-mark hypothesis plus duplicate reproduction. A locale/font comparison is the next step.
evidence: Reported on 0.65.0 in Simplified Chinese Windows 11 with Microsoft YaHei UI and the Pinyin subset.
The author explicitly supplied that font and subset after being asked.
A commenter attributes missing combining-diacritic glyphs to YaHei/JhengHei versus Segoe UI; this remains an unverified font-coverage claim.
#33189 was closed as a duplicate and gives Chinese-language Pinyin/All plus m as a concrete test.
judgment.recommended_action: Verify current Quick Accent rendering under Chinese font fallback, then approve a scoped glyph-font correction if still needed.

fix_assessment.rationale: A UI font/fallback change may address combining-character rendering. No matching public fix was found; current UI changes make a current-build baseline necessary.

proposed_fixes.title: Render Quick Accent combining sequences with verified font coverage
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the locale-inherited UI font/fallback does not render the combined Pinyin sequence as intended. The current selector's candidate TextBlock has no explicit FontFamily, but current runtime fallback has not been measured.
plan: Compare candidate glyph rendering under Simplified/Traditional Chinese and English using the exact combining sequences from the report and #33189.

If inherited font selection is responsible, apply an explicit verified glyph-capable font/fallback only to candidate display text, retaining localized labels and preserving inserted Unicode sequences.
Add coverage for combining marks, multi-codepoint characters, theme/scale variants and locale changes; do not replace characters or normalize inserted text solely to hide a display defect.
verification: Pinyin ɑ plus U+0304 and the m combining-mark candidates render without missing-glyph boxes in Chinese locales.
Copy or insert each sequence and verify its code points are unchanged.
Check English, Chinese labels, selected-candidate contrast and high-DPI sizing.

confidence.rationale: The explicit locale/font reply and duplicate are strong, but actual font coverage and current UI fallback need a runtime comparison.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent shows malformed or missing combining-character glyphs in a Chinese Windows environment; the font, subset and a more recent duplicate test are already available.
known_information: The original screenshot shows the failure for ɑ with a combining macron.
The author identified Microsoft YaHei UI and Pinyin on Simplified Chinese Windows 11 Home China.
The 2024 discussion identifies combining-diacritic coverage as a possible cause and compares Segoe UI.
The issue is open with Needs-Repro, but the earlier font/subset question was answered; it is not waiting on that reply.
inferences: Font selection/fallback is more plausible than an unsupported character mapping, but missing codepoint claims require actual font inspection.
The current WinUI-based selector may behave differently from the historical build, so resolution cannot be inferred from old evidence alone.
issue_context.analysis: A maintainer can reproduce with Chinese locale and the supplied sequences. Do not ask the reporter again for the font or subset or misrepresent the already answered request as author waiting.
initial_investigation: Read the body and all four comments and exhausted the timeline; inspected duplicate #33189, which adds Chinese Pinyin/All and m test instructions.

Located and inspected src/modules/poweraccent/PowerAccent.UI/PowerAccentXAML/SelectorControl.xaml at main commit 3d6827a53a579ba9bedcf8d4bbda21348d78cbdb: candidate TextBlock uses bound text and FontSize 18 without an explicit FontFamily.
The current MainWindow.xaml hosts SelectorControl, so the candidate template, not the outer window, is the relevant display surface.
No font binary inspection or Chinese-locale rendering test was performed.

reproduce.title: Verify combining-mark rendering without changing inserted text
reproduce.version_requirement: Current supported build; compare historical 0.65.0/0.81.1 only if needed in isolated testing.
prerequisites: A Chinese Windows test account or VM with Microsoft YaHei UI; add Traditional Chinese/JhengHei and English controls when available.
Enable Pinyin or All in Quick Accent.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Prepare a text sample containing U+0251 followed by U+0304 (ɑ̄), plus the m combining-diacritic candidates from Quick Accent's Pinyin set. Provide a code-point listing so display comparisons never silently normalize or replace the sequence.
steps: 1. Select Chinese for PowerToys and enable the Pinyin subset; open candidates for the reported sequence and m.
2. Compare the same sequence in the Quick Accent candidate template under the inherited font and a verified Segoe UI test font.
3. Repeat under English and, if available, Traditional Chinese to separate locale and font effects.
4. Insert the selected character into a Unicode-aware text editor and compare exact code points.
5. Check selected/unselected candidate rendering under light, dark, high contrast and increased display scaling.
reproduce.expected_result: Candidate combining sequences render legibly without missing-glyph boxes, localized labels remain correct, and inserted code points are unchanged.
